It is the contractor half of Kofi Silva converting from contractor (C5001) to employee (E1023), starting today. Both records share the same government ID token, and E1023 shows it was converted from C5001. Our policy is to carry the identity over, so the plan moves the existing account to the new record. It does not treat this as a leaver.

**What the plan does:**
- **Identity:** Re-point account acct-1a16daff to E1023 (WID 0d1db84897623f4094c16aad0575665b) as an Employee. It keeps the same login name and email address (kofi.silva@example.com), access groups, licence, mailbox and current session. His groups already match the Software Engineer standard access, with no conflicting permissions, so no group changes are needed.
- **Workday:** Write kofi.silva@example.com back to E1023 and confirm it went through. Then mark both onboarding tasks complete:

  - **"Provision equipment":** his engineering laptop bundle from ticket tkt-eq-C5001 is already delivered and stays with him. Ordering again would duplicate it, so the plan marks this task complete without a new order. That is a judgement call, because the existing order sits under his contractor record.
- **Finance:** Create a finance profile for E1023 with cost center CC-1000 and Jordan Carter as expense approver. His open expense report exp-2e87d415 (988, pending) is already with Jordan Carter, who is active, so it is left to be approved as normal.

**What the plan deliberately does not do** (all things a normal termination would trigger):
- No disabling the account, ending sessions, removing access or licences, or changing the mailbox.
- No new account (the email address is taken by his existing account).
- No equipment recovery, no closing his expense reports, no final pay request.
- No card deactivation: his contractor card is already inactive.

Nothing needs a human decision. Neither record has a legal hold, and there are no other events in the feed.
